Caption: 

Welcome, humans. 

Alphabet shares [fell 9%](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/02/04/alphabet-q4-earnings-report-2024.html) yesterday after it announced a revenue miss and a cool $75B in new AI capex. Google’s CFO said the company’s data centers ended the year with “more demand than we had available capacity”, which could explain both those issues. 

Google also used the earnings call to flex their Gemini 2.0 Flash and Flash Thinking models as “[some of the most efficient out there](https://www.marketwatch.com/livecoverage/alphabet-earnings-stock-google-results-ai-cloud-youtube/card/google-s-management-has-some-thoughts-on-the-deepseek-developments-8zCOGWzAjPvV8KnxmOvP)”, even compared to DeepSeek and R1. And yet, they STILL can’t meet demand. Classic [Jevons paradox](https://www.npr.org/sections/planet-money/2025/02/04/g-s1-46018/ai-deepseek-economics-jevons-paradox), am I right? 

AMD, NVIDIA’s rival, also [reported earnings](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/02/04/amd-earnings-report-q4-2024.html), and even though its data center chip sales doubled in 2024, it still missed expectations. 

Data centers just can’t catch a break these days. One minute there’s not enough, the next minute, still not enough—I mean, what are we going to do, give them _more than two minutes_ to catch up? 

**Here’s what you need to know about AI today:**

* ByteDance demo’d the ultimate deepfake tool. 

* Cloudflare added Adobe image verification across its network.

* Google dropped AI weapons restriction from its principles.

* Robot startup Figure AI leaves OpenAI, claims its own breakthrough.

Advertise in The Neuron here. (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfng1Qz3wGLc_-f9goa1TQgnGE_rehbW55Gx5VaEYIhn4OueQ/viewform)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8725d956-e5e7-4b68-90a6-08a1aaebeacf/Neuron-Page-Splitters3.png)
Caption: 

# Deepfakes are about to get out of control…like _10x better_ out of control. 

Ever wished you could make that old photo of your grandma sing “Happy Birthday”? Or turn your LinkedIn headshot into a TED talk? Or, IDK, create a realistic version of yourself to attend Zoom meetings while you’re sipping Mai Tai’s in Honolulu? 

**Well, ByteDance (TikTok's parent company)’s ****[new AI model](https://omnihuman-lab.github.io/)**** can do exactly that, and TBH, it’s sorta terrifying.**

It’s called [OmniHuman-1](https://omnihuman-lab.github.io/), and it takes any photo—selfies, full-body shots, even cartoons—and makes it move realistically based on both audio or video inputs. And, unlike previous models, it works with pretty much any kind of image ([paper here](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.01061)). 

Here are [10 incredible examples](https://x.com/ai_for_success/status/1886685232952435133)—can you guess which is [our favorite](https://x.com/ai_for_success/status/1886686901505286232)? Shockingly, it’s NOT [this clip](https://youtu.be/GGTcVOb2S9k) of Taylor Swift singing a Naruto theme song, or [THIS clip](https://x.com/ai_for_success/status/1886686919368827135) of Jensen Huang rapping…_but that was a close second._

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1102afa8-8a3a-4da2-901b-60b2a60aeb38/Screenshot_2025-02-04_at_4.15.56_PM_1.png?t=1738714661)
Follow image link: (https://x.com/ai_for_success/status/1886685232952435133)
Caption: 

**What makes OmniHuman-1 special is its versatility:**

* Creates eerily realistic gestures and expressions.

* Handles both singing and talking naturally.

* Even works with non-human objects.

Think of it like a universal translator between still images and motion. You feed it a photo and some audio, and it figures out how to make that photo move naturally with the sound. 

**See, China isn’t just leading the open-source AI race for **[**reasoning models**](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/american-vs-chinese-ai)**…** with Tuesday’s release of [OmniHuman-1](https://omnihuman-lab.github.io/), and previous leading video models like [Hunyuan](https://aivideo.hunyuan.tencent.com/), [Kling](https://www.klingai.com/), and [MiniMax](https://hailuoai.video/), it’s clear the country is heavily focused on video content, too

**And this is just one piece of the synthetic media explosion:**

NVIDIA-backed [Synthesia](https://www.synthesia.io/) just raised a [new round of $180M](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/01/15/ai-video-platform-synthesia-doubles-valuation-to-2point1-billion.html) that values the company at $2.1B and now has [60K customers](https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/14/synthesia-snaps-up-180m-on-a-2-1b-valuation-for-its-b2b-ai-video-platform/). It and [HeyGen](https://www.heygen.com/) (who [raised $60M](https://www.heygen.com/article/announcing-our-series-a)) are the two leading avatar startups, and for good reason—they _look good_. 

Gone are the days of wonky static avatars; these tools now provide [motion control](https://x.com/HeyGen_Official/status/1882617401994625198) and other features that make their avatars more realistic than ever. 

Synthesia gets its realistic voices from [ElevenLabs](https://elevenlabs.io/), the leading voice AI who just raised its [own round of $180M](https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/30/elevenlabs-raises-180-million-in-series-c-funding-at-3-3-billion-valuation/) at a valuation of $3.3B. There’s also [Cartesia](https://cartesia.ai/?utm_source=theneuron), who makes an incredibly life-like voice AI called Sonic ([demo here](https://x.com/EHuanglu/status/1886439926721605801)). 

**All of these companies want to become **_**more **_**lifelike.** You look at their roadmaps, and that’s basically what’s coming—moving AI from [the uncanny valley](https://spectrum.ieee.org/what-is-the-uncanny-valley) to the _make money valley. _

The problem? The most profitable use for life-like avatars is deepfakes, either used to [influence elections](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/04/deepfake-videos-are-getting-shockingly-good/) or scam people and corporations [out of billions](https://www2.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/financial-services-industry-predictions/2024/deepfake-banking-fraud-risk-on-the-rise.html). And if scammers get access to tools like OmniHuman-1 to play with? I think [Darth Vader said it best](https://youtu.be/ONBAMgTC4dw?feature=shared)…

# Prompt Tip of the Day 

Robin Delta just [dropped 7 killer prompts](https://x.com/heyrobinai/status/1886355123544441252) for o3-mini + search to master any topic without spending a dime on courses.

**Our favorite?** The “[_Socratic Enlightenment_](https://x.com/heyrobinai/status/1886355020893040839)” prompt transforms o3 into your personal Socrates. Instead of just info-dumping, it guides you through deep, probing questions that actually stick in your brain. Super useful for challenging concepts.

**Pro tip:** After (_Bill and Ted voice)_ _[So-crates](https://youtu.be/xkfvg1j1yg8?feature=shared)__-_GPT guides your learning, run the “[Teach-back Mastery](https://x.com/heyrobinai/status/1886355053235372165)” prompt to teach the concept you just learned back to o3. o3 will spot any gaps in your understanding, and help you patch them up. _Party on, dudes!!!_
